hook.text: Body is how coffee feels in your mouth—thin like tea, or thick like cream. It's a texture, not a flavor.

buildup.text: Oils and suspended solids create body. Metal filters let oils through; paper filters trap them.

discovery.text: French press coffee has heavy body because the metal mesh lets oils and fine particles into your cup.

twist.text: Espresso has the heaviest body of all—emulsified oils under pressure create a syrupy, coating texture.

climax.text: Brew method determines body more than bean choice. The same bean can feel thin or thick depending on method.

punchline.text: Flavor is what you taste. Body is what you feel. Both matter.

quiz.question: Why does French press coffee have more body than pour-over?
options: The metal mesh lets oils and particles through
